baseline.note: Historical report counts. No new live coverage reduction is claimed.

fixes.implementation: Bounded activity inspection distinguishes visible, provably inactive and unverified registered scopes. A single visible provider can be selected only when every competing matched scope is inactive. Didomi is scoped to its host/notice, not marketing classes. Ambiguous and zero-size cases remain unresolved.

Canonical exact contextual Manage Settings label; Termly primary action-area selection with legacy fallback; versioned Cookiebot and Termly exact aria-controls deferred panel bindings. One Options action, unique original root, accessible named panel and document binding remain mandatory.
Preference inspection uses the legacy banner or official UI-v2 shadow host, excluding marketing navigation. No arbitrary popup or new cross-root action recipe was introduced.

Borlabs service accounting is independent of malformed, unavailable or truncated cookie declarations. Verified service names survive; incomplete cookie inventories cannot establish missing declarations.
Canonical materialization retains a missing-evidence explanation and interprets existing paired-capture deferral diagnostics. Pixel allowance, scheduling and visual-finding eligibility are unchanged.

remaining: Fresh EU-Ireland captures are required to measure coverage gains; the previous public sample remains on its contact cooldown.
Iubenda UI-v2 popup transition and TrustArc preference-panel binding need retained structural proof before additional navigation can be authorized.
Didomi may still have no actionable first-layer visitor CMP, even after installed-SDK ambiguity is separated.
Partial cookie inventories, unavailable declaration purposes and unmeasured prominence remain explicitly incomplete or unassessed.

cost.basis: Bounded DOM reads and small diagnostics inside existing lane deadlines. No new lane, invocation, model call, retention policy or standing capacity. Estimate is not a production measurement.

sources.use: UI-v2 shadow banner and Preferences event; insufficient by itself to authorize an arbitrary popup
